We have received your message that asks to join the International Alliance. Your reason to join The I.A is to help dissolve conflicts, promote trade, and solve the problem of communication and corruption. The I.A's purpose is to do exactly this, and we'd be happy to accept you. This means that your request has been [b]accepted[/b], and you are a fully fledged member of the International Alliance. You will be added onto the list of I.A members shortly.

[b]Extra info for the members.[/b]

Feel free to give any feedback about the I.A in the telegrams. remember that [nation]New Westmore[/nation], [nation]Indonocaismnic[/nation]/[nation]Oceanice Republic[/nation], [nation]United Hydronia[/nation], and [nation]Sikirsk[/nation] are all founders of the I.A, so you can send your feedback to them as well. In cordone's discord, we have a channel dedicated to the I.A, so if you have Discord, you should check it out.

You may also submit a vote into the International Alliance, so that people may discuss that issue, and pass the vote. These votes act as rules, meaning if the vote passes, all member nations will have to follow those rules. You may write this proposal with no restrictions, but it is up to the member nations to vote for it. Member nations may vote against the proposal if it is too strict. In the International Alliance, there are a council of six nations. This council of nations are the strongest in Erene, and are considered a superpower. These nations may completely veto a vote if they want. All member nations may enact the proposal for their own nation anyway even if it gets declined.[/quote]

[spoiler= The Rebirth (Part 1) ~1000 Words]
The winds blew cold that morning, sharp and restless like old ghosts howling over the black waters of Lake Ilinalta. In the throne hall of Bondahall, the heart of Heiðabýr, all was still. Ancient timber beams groaned softly in the wind, and the flickering torchlight cast long, wavering shadows across the basalt floor. High King Jorik III Blodskald sat high upon the throne of wood and silver, his pale eyes fixed on the war table before him.
The Althing, the assembly of jarls, his ministers and military advisors, stood in grim silence. No one dared speak, not while the High King studied the papers laid bare like offerings at a sacred rite. One parchment in particular drew his eye: marked with the red wax seal of the Elseyran Geostrategic Resources Organization, it bore dire significance. The High King's expression hardened as he read.
The air in the hall was heavy with tension. After several long minutes, Jorik raised his gaze.
This land called..Chernarus, he began, voice calculated and cold like ice. What is it worth?
Jarl Holmgeir of Reykjavik, the Minister of Industry and chief economic advisor, cleared his throat nervously before stepping forward.
Our analysts believe the uranium deposits in the eastern mountains of Chernarus are among the highest concentrations recorded in Elseyr. At least 140,000 tons of extractable ore. Enough to restart our nuclear program from the ground upreactors, weapons, research. If harnessed correctly, it could propel our GDP beyond six trillion within twelve months.
Murmurs broke out across the chamberwords of wealth, power, and fear. Even those who usually remained stoic, like Jarl Freyderic of Warangia or the hardened Marshal Hjallmarsson, found themselves whispering possibilities. But not Jorik. His face remained still.
He remembered the days when the world bowed its head to the White Dragon of the North. When Jomslandic fleets prowled the seas like iron sea monsters, and foreign kings paid tribute in fear, not friendship. But those days had passed. The Commonwealth remained proud, yet its enemies had grown faster, richer, more dangerous. Superpowers with atomic arsenals now loomed across the world like gods of ash and fire.
And Jomsland, once the storm, had become the silence.
Not anymore.
Summon my generals, Jorik ordered quietly. And tell them to prepare the fleet.
One week later, Operation Magna Teutonia was signed into law under the Sovereign Authority Clause. The full details were known only to the High King, the war council, and a select few within the Jomslandic Intelligence Organization.
At dawn, under the veil of dense fog rolling across Lake Ilinalta, Jomsland made its move.
Surveillance drones crossed the strait first, quiet, helicopter-looking machines flying silently through the fog. They mapped the terrain, tagged infrastructure targets, and intercepted military frequencies. Beneath them, trawler ships moved through the lake, civilian vessels on paper, but beneath the surface, they bristled with sensors, jammer arrays, and concealed commando teams.
Simultaneously, the Jomsviking Order, Jomslands most elite special forces, men trained in arctic survival, urban infiltration, and asymmetric warfare, were deployed across the lands via eithet smugglers or rotorcraft drop. By the time local radar realized what was happening, it was already too late.
But the true assault did not begin with bombs.
It began with silence.
In less than twenty minutes, the Jomslandic Cyber Security Forces unleashed an electromagnetic and data-warfare strike across Chernaruss digital infrastructure. Power grids failed. Satellites were blinded. Command networks were severed. Phones went dead. Drones fell from the sky. For a crucial half-hour, Chernarus was blind, deaf, and paralyzed.
Then came the thunder.
Precision cruise missiles struck military depots, radar arrays, and airfields. Coastal towns found themselves occupied by amphibious assault teams wearing modern black and dark blue armor and bearing the White Dragon sigil. Resistance was minimal, most of the local defense militias surrendered on sight, others fled inland. A few pledged allegiance in exchange for protection from their own fractured regime.
Within two weeks, over sixty percent of Chernarus was under Jomslandic control. The capital had not yet fallen, but its outer districts were already in chaos. The uranium-rich highlands in the east were surrounded, though not yet secured. And in them, the real war began.
Guerrilla fighters emerged from forests and mines, striking supply lines, ambushing convoys, using the terrain with deadly familiarity. Mines were rigged with traps. Extraction efforts slowed. Jomsland's commanders, though seasoned, found themselves in a grinding war of attrition.
Outside Elseyr, condemnation followed. Several neutral nations decried Jomsland's actions as a "resource war of aggression." Others warned of economic sanctions. A few hinted at military aid to Chernarus. The pressure mounted.
But Jorik was unmoved.
Appearing before the Althing in a rare live address, the High King looked every inch the warrior-ruler of old: cloaked in the pelts of northern wolves, steel armor supporting his crippled leg, and the ancient axe of Jom Blodskald laid across his lap.
We do not invade to conquer, he declared, voice steady and defiant. We invade to survive.
Long ago, the world feared us and its time that this fear returns. We watched as others grew rich and more, while we did nothing. No more.
We rise not to threaten, but to remain.
And with that, Jomsland shifted the narrative.
Envoys were dispatched to the remaining Chernarusian leadership, those who hadnt fled or been killed. A proposal was made: a protectorate arrangement, jointly managed with Elseyran Defense Union oversight. Chernarus would be granted internal autonomy within five years, and the people would be guaranteed security, food, and rebuilding efforts.
Simultaneously, high-speed construction began on the Wadruna-Prime Reactor Complex, named after the goddess Wadruna the Storm Mother Located near the richest uranium veins, it was guarded around the clock by automated turrets, drone patrols, and a garrison of nearly two thousand soldiers. Extraction had resumed, and the first shipments were already crossing the lake under naval escort.
Whatever the world said, Jomsland had moved. The dragon stirred once more. And far to the east, other powers watched the jomslandic sails on the lakes black waters with renewed caution.
The age of silence was ending.[/spoiler]
Part 1 of my Expansion
